name: Fence Repair vs Fence Replacement

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a fence repair and a full fence replacement?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between a fence repair and a full fence replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fence repair is appropriate when the damage is limited and the main structure is still sound. Examples include replacing a few boards, resetting one or two posts, fixing hardware, or patching a small section after wind or impact damage. Full replacement is usually the better choice when many posts are failing, the fence is rotting throughout, the line is uneven, or repairs would be repeated every season. In Los Angeles County, sun exposure, dry rot, termites, and wind can all shorten a fence’s life. Ask the contractor to separate cosmetic damage from structural failure and to estimate how much of the fence will still need attention within the next few years. That makes the repair-versus-replace choice much clearer.
acceptedAnswer.description: Fence repair fixes isolated problems such as broken boards, damaged panels, leaning posts, or a small section of rot. Full replacement is better when the posts are failing, damage is widespread, or the fence is too old to repair cost-effectively. If the structure is unstable, replacing only the surface parts usually does not solve the problem.
